nameStory: The 'five-leaved' part of this shrub's name comes from its distinctive hand-shaped leaves that typically have five leaflets spreading out like fingers. The 'chaste tree' name has ancient roots - these plants were traditionally believed to suppress desire and were grown in monastery gardens, earning them a reputation as symbols of chastity and purity.
description: The five-leaved chaste tree is an aromatic shrub or small tree that can grow anywhere from 6 to 26 feet tall. It has distinctive hand-shaped leaves with five pointed leaflets and reddish-brown bark. In summer, it produces showy clusters of small white to blue flowers that give off a pleasant fragrance, followed by small dark berries in fall.

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: Hand-shaped leaves with usually five pointed, toothed leaflets that feel soft and fuzzy underneath due to dense hairs - like touching velvet

idTips.label: Flowers
idTips.description: Dense, upright clusters of small white to blue flowers, each about 2-3 inches long, with fuzzy petals of different lengths giving an irregular, lopsided look

idTips.label: Bark
idTips.description: Distinctive reddish-brown bark that stands out against the silvery-white fuzzy branches

idTips.label: Growth Habit
idTips.description: Grows as an upright, somewhat irregular shrub with square-shaped branches covered in dense white fuzz

idTips.label: Fruit/Seeds
idTips.description: Small round berries about the size of a peppercorn that turn from green to black or purple when ripe

habitat: This is an extremely rare plant in New England, with only one documented observation in the region. As a native of Asia that's occasionally planted in gardens, you'd most likely encounter it as an ornamental shrub in residential areas or botanical collections rather than growing wild.

seasonality.spring: New leaves emerge with their characteristic fuzzy, silvery appearance on the undersides. The distinctive hand-shaped leaf pattern becomes evident.
seasonality.summer: Peak blooming season with fragrant flower clusters appearing at branch tips. The plant is most easily identified during this time.
seasonality.fall: Small dark berries ripen to black or purple. Leaves may begin to yellow before dropping.
seasonality.winter: Bare branches show the distinctive square shape with fuzzy white coating, and reddish-brown bark becomes more prominent.

funFact: This plant is like nature's aromatherapy kit - every part of it is fragrant! The leaves, flowers, and even the branches release a pleasant, spicy scent when touched or brushed against, which is why it's been treasured in traditional medicine for thousands of years.
confusionNotes: The hand-shaped leaves might remind you of marijuana or a buckeye, but five-leaved chaste tree's leaves are much fuzzier underneath and the whole plant has that distinctive aromatic smell. Plus, the upright flower clusters and square, fuzzy branches are dead giveaways.
contextualKnowledge: Despite being called a 'chaste tree,' this plant isn't actually a true tree in the botanical sense - it's more of a large shrub in the mint family. Don't let the name fool you into thinking it's related to other trees; it's actually a cousin to herbs like basil and lavender!
compareHints: While its relative the lilac chaste tree (Vitex agnus-castus) has similar hand-shaped leaves, the five-leaved chaste tree typically has five leaflets versus the lilac chaste tree's seven. The five-leaved species also tends to have more silvery, fuzzy foliage and slightly smaller flower clusters, making it look more delicate overall.

relatedSpecies.distinction: The only other chaste tree you might encounter is five-leaved chaste tree (Vitex negundo), but it's even rarer in New England.
